title: Evidence Bureau: The One-Person Software Business
summary: An original, offline claim/evidence map investigating whether a solo founder can operate a useful AI-majority software business. Nine inspected public sources, a pre-collection protocol, explicit opposing cases, source drilldowns, seven operating gates and falsifiable reversal conditions keep coding productivity distinct from verified business viability.
limitations: Conditional plausibility, not a proven broad business claim, market test, financial audit, success-rate estimate or universal impossibility result.
Coding benchmarks, task completion and enterprise throughput are implementation proxies, not direct evidence of paying demand, retained use, complete owner economics or solo operations.
Commercial claims retain founder/acquirer attribution; nine documents are six provenance families, not independent votes.
Primary source dates span historical tools and populations. The METR 2026 methodological update prevents treating its 2025 slowdown as a current constant.
Eight raw HTTP body hashes are retained. News18 succeeded through web_fetch but direct capture returned 403, so only bounded tool-returned excerpts and their local artifact hash are available.
Automated checks cover data, provenance, links, UI logic and counterfactual verdict rules; no real-browser visual certification or human review is claimed.
The seed's eighteen synthetic observations are separately labeled and hash-verified; no downloaded seed code, native initialization, server, external mutation, publication or outreach was performed.
